info.tips.title: Safe handover tips
info.terms.0.title: A little campus teamwork
info.terms.0.body: Zarqa is a student-made lost-and-found service for the GUtech community. It isn't run by GUtech and isn't an official university channel, though the GUtech RSA desk helps with items handed in there. Using Zarqa means you agree to these terms and to the Privacy notice.
info.terms.1.title: Who can use it
info.terms.1.body: You need to be 18 or older and sign in with your own GUtech email. If you're under 18, hand in or ask about items at the RSA desk in person instead. One account per person, and keep your sign-in codes to yourself.
info.terms.2.title: Keep it honest
info.terms.2.body: Only post things you really lost or found, and only share photos and details you have the right to share. Don't claim someone else's property, pretend to be someone else, harass anyone or post unlawful content. Oman's laws apply, including the Cyber Crime Law. We may close reports or suspend accounts that break these rules, and may report serious misuse to GUtech or the authorities.
info.terms.3.title: A match is a suggestion
info.terms.3.body: AI can miss items or suggest the wrong one. Check identifying details before handing anything over. Zarqa doesn't hold items (only the RSA desk does, for things handed in there), verify ownership, guarantee a return or arrange the handover for you. Meet safely and never pay to unlock a match.
info.terms.4.title: No guarantees
info.terms.4.body: Zarqa is free, run by a student, and provided as it is, with no guarantees. It may change, pause or stop. As far as the law allows, we aren’t responsible for lost, damaged or wrongly returned items, or for what happens when users meet.
info.terms.5.title: Changes, leaving and the law
info.terms.5.body: If these terms or the Privacy notice change in a way that matters, Zarqa asks you to agree again before you carry on. You can leave any time: close your reports or delete your account in Profile. These terms are governed by the laws of the Sultanate of Oman. Questions or a report of misuse: email hello@tryzarqa.com.
info.privacy.0.title: Who's responsible
info.privacy.0.body: Zarqa is run by a GUtech student (the operator), who is responsible for your data (the data controller) and also acts as its data protection officer. Zarqa isn't run by GUtech. For any privacy question or request, email hello@tryzarqa.com.
info.privacy.1.title: What we collect
info.privacy.1.body:
We collect:
- your university email, first name, profile settings and optional profile photo
- your lost and found reports, their photos, match results and matching logs
- chats, handover details and read markers
- if you turn on push alerts, your browser’s push subscription

Uploaded photos are re-encoded with their location and camera data (EXIF) removed. Sign-in uses one session cookie and short-lived sign-in codes. There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking cookies.
info.privacy.2.title: Why we use it
info.privacy.2.body: Only to run the lost-and-found: to sign you in, match lost and found reports, let owners and finders talk and arrange handovers, work with the RSA desk, send you the emails and alerts the service needs, and keep it safe from misuse. We never sell your data and never send marketing or advertising.
info.privacy.3.title: Your consent
info.privacy.3.body: We use your data because you expressly agree to it. Zarqa asks for that consent, and records when you gave it and to which version, before you can use the service. That includes processing outside Oman (see below). You can withdraw consent at any time by deleting your account in Profile or emailing us. Zarqa is for people aged 18 or older. If RSA desk staff file a report for you at your request, Zarqa asks for your consent when you first sign in.
info.privacy.4.title: Who can see it?
info.privacy.4.body:
There is no public list of reports. Who sees what:
- The person who lost an item: possible matches for their report, with ordinary photos and covered card photos.
- Owner and finder: once the owner says an item could be theirs, a private chat between the two of them. Your profile photo shows there only while your first name does; with your name hidden you appear as “GUtech student”, with no photo.
- GUtech RSA desk staff: owner–finder chats (read-only, to keep handovers safe), and every found report with its photos and the finder’s first name (if shown). When someone claims an item at the desk, they also see the owner’s first name and description. If you ask for an item at the desk, staff can file a lost report for you under your GUtech email.
- Admins: reports, owner emails, photos (card photos only covered) and matching logs, to moderate the service. The operator has server access for maintenance.

Photos of cards and IDs are first covered on our own server by text recognition (OCR) that hides every number, machine-readable line and barcode it finds; names, faces and logos stay visible. Only that covered copy is ever shown: to a possible owner while they decide, to the finder or owner after a claim, to RSA staff and to admins. If covering fails or any number is still readable, the photo stays visible only to its uploader, and the original is never shown to anyone else.
info.privacy.5.title: Processing outside Oman
info.privacy.5.body:
Zarqa needs providers outside Oman to work:
- Contabo (Europe) hosts our server.
- OpenAI (United States) reads report text and permitted photos to find matches.
- DeepSeek (China) and TypeSafe step in only when the main AI is unavailable.
- Resend (United States) sends our emails.
- Your browser’s push service delivers alerts you turn on.

Original card and ID photos never go to any provider: the covering runs on our own server. We chose providers we believe protect data to a standard comparable to Oman’s law. Please don’t write identity numbers, bank details, or health or other sensitive details in reports.
info.privacy.6.title: How long?
info.privacy.6.body:
- Open reports expire after 60 days without an update.
- Finished reports (returned, expired or closed), their photos and chats are deleted about six months (182 days) after that.
- Matching logs are kept for up to 182 days, even after you delete your account.
- Accounts stay until you delete them.
- Nightly server backups are kept for 14 days.
- Found items handed in at the RSA desk stay listed until the RSA closes them, because the item is still on their shelf.

Cleanup runs daily, so removal isn’t instant.
info.privacy.7.title: Your rights
info.privacy.7.body:
Under Oman’s Personal Data Protection Law you can:
- withdraw your consent
- ask us to correct, update or block your data
- get a copy of it, or have it sent to another provider
- have it deleted

Much of this you can do in the app: change your name, photo and settings in Profile, close or delete your reports, or use Profile › Delete my account, which removes your account, reports, photos, chats and alerts from the live service. For anything else, email hello@tryzarqa.com: we reply within 45 days, free of charge. If you think your data was handled unlawfully, you can complain to the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology (linked at the end of this notice).
info.privacy.8.title: Keeping it safe
info.privacy.8.body: Connections are encrypted (HTTPS), the server is locked down to the operator, and backups can be read only by the operator. Only the people described above can see your data. If a breach puts your data at risk, we'll tell the Ministry and you within 72 hours of finding out, with what happened and what we're doing about it.
info.privacy.9.title: Changes to this notice
info.privacy.9.body: If this notice changes in a way that matters, Zarqa asks for your consent again before you carry on. This version is dated 13 November 2026.
info.help.0.title: Lost something?
info.help.0.body: Post a lost report from Home. Add the brand, colour, identifying marks and where and when you last had it. Zarqa looks for possible matches: check My reports, and turn on Match alerts in Profile so you hear about them. If nothing shows up yet, check My reports again later or ask at the RSA desk.
info.help.1.title: Found something?
info.help.1.body: Post a found report. You can keep the item and meet the owner: when the owner says an item could be theirs, a chat opens so you can check ownership and arrange a handover. Or switch on “I’ll drop it at the RSA desk”, take it there and show your drop code; the owner collects it from the RSA desk with a pickup code, no chat needed. When the item is back with its owner, tap “I handed it over” in the chat; the owner confirms with “I got it back”.
info.help.2.title: Something feels off?
info.help.2.body: For a bug, mistaken claim, abusive message, privacy request or feedback, email hello@tryzarqa.com. Include a report reference if useful, but never send bank-card details, identity documents or sign-in codes. This inbox is not an emergency service.
info.help.3.title: Can’t sign in?
info.help.3.body: Use your GUtech email. The 6-digit code usually arrives within a minute: check your junk or spam folder too. A code works for 10 minutes; if it runs out, ask for a new one. Still stuck? Email hello@tryzarqa.com.
info.help.4.title: Not getting alerts?
info.help.4.body:
Turn on Match alerts in Profile, then allow notifications when your phone asks. With Match alerts on, match emails arrive even without phone alerts, but chat messages only reach you as alerts or in the app.

- On iPhone, alerts only work once Zarqa is on your Home Screen: open it in Safari, tap Share, then “Add to Home Screen”, and open Zarqa from there.
- If notifications are blocked, allow them for Zarqa in your browser or phone settings, then check Profile again.
info.tips.0.title: Meet where people are
info.tips.0.body: Choose a busy campus spot in daylight. Bring a friend if that feels better. Use chat to agree on a place and time, then confirm the handover.
info.tips.1.title: Check the little details
info.tips.1.body: Ask the person to describe a detail you haven’t shared, such as a sticker or what’s inside a case. A match, even a BIG CHANCE one, is a clue, not proof of ownership.
info.tips.2.title: Keep private things private
info.tips.2.body: Don’t share identity numbers, bank-card details, passwords or sign-in codes. For an ID or card, describe it without copying its numbers. Its uploaded photo is shown to others only with the numbers covered.
info.tips.3.title: No pressure, no payments
info.tips.3.body: Don’t pay a fee or follow an unfamiliar link to claim an item. If something feels wrong, stop the handover and email hello@tryzarqa.com. Once the item is safely back, tap “I got it back” in the chat so Zarqa can stop searching.
